## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C IPO and TRA execution

- 2020-10-05: Form-of TRA first filed as S-1 Exhibit 10.3 (WTM party listed as the Luxembourg subsidiary)
- 2020-10-23: Form-of re-filed in S-1/A No. 3 with WTM party rewritten to the Bermuda parent
- 2020-10-27: TRA executed at IPO close; 8-K Exhibit 10.2 carries the executed instrument

#### Valuation-allowance period

- 2021-2022: Class A price collapses from ~$60 to single digits; full valuation allowance keeps TRA liability at zero on the balance sheet; contract not amended

#### First Amendment

- 2023-10-01: First Amendment effective; LIBOR-to-SOFR transition (Agreed/Default/Early Termination Rates), state-tax-allocation methodology refinement, governance plumbing (Section 7.18 Participant Representatives); 85% rate, beneficiaries, and attributes unchanged

#### Payment phase resumes

- 2023-Q1: First cash payment of $2.8M (2021 tax year)
- 2024: Profitability returns; valuation allowance released; YE2024 current portion accrued
- 2025-12-31: Liability $131.1M
- 2026-Q1: $7.0M payment (2024 tax year); Mar 31 2026 liability $123.4M

## Explanation

MediaAlpha, Inc. executed the TRA on October 27, 2020 at its Up-C IPO close, agreeing to pay 85% of cash tax savings to two beneficiary sub-groups under distinct attribute pools: White Mountains Insurance Group, Ltd. on utilization of Intermediate Holdco pre-IPO NOLs (plus certain imputed interest), and the Step-Up Participants (Insignia Capital affiliates and Senior Executives including Steven Yi, Eugene Nonko, and Tigran Sinanyan) on Section 732/734(b)/743(b)/755 basis step-ups arising from exchanges of Class B-1 units. The 2021-2022 stock-price collapse drove a full valuation allowance on the related deferred tax assets and zero recorded TRA liability through 2022, but the contract was never amended or terminated in response; the October 1, 2023 First Amendment was an administrative LIBOR-to-SOFR transition with state-tax-allocation refinements and governance plumbing, not a re-pricing. As profitability returned in 2024, MediaAlpha released the valuation allowance, re-determined payments as probable, and the liability re-emerged at full size: $131.1M at YE2025 and $123.4M at March 31, 2026 after a $7.0M Q1 2026 payment for the 2024 tax year. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
